hero: What does it cost to keep your data?
intro: Start with 10 GB of new orders per year. Change one storage decision at a time.
storageOnly: Storage only. Requests, restores, transfers, and queries are billed separately.
policy: Archive at day 90, expire at day 365
context: Annual CSV input: {{volume}}. Monthly savings are compared with {{cost}} for uncompressed CSV in S3 Northern Virginia, kept for your selected retention period.
matrixFine: The first two columns use your retention period. The 90/365-day policy keeps one year and archives after 90 days. The last column uses your archive and retention settings. Monthly costs assume the retention window is full; 1 year = 365 days.
archiveFine: Transitions, restores, and per-object archive metadata can change the bill, especially with many small files.
modelBody: The volume is new uncompressed CSV per year. Monthly storage is estimated at steady state: annual bytes × retention years, adjusted by the measured format ratio. Years use 365 days. Records older than the archive threshold move to archive until their retention period ends. Bytes are converted into 2³⁰-byte billing units. Both Before and After use your retention period; Before keeps everything in S3 Standard Northern Virginia. Format ratios come from 100,000 synthetic orders.
modelHold: If you also keep the original CSV, add its storage cost to the estimate.
lesson0.name: Baseline
lesson0.title: Start with the orders export
lesson0.description: One CSV contains dates, customer details, SKUs, and amounts. Choose how much new data arrives each year. Retention determines how many years remain stored.
lesson0.detail: At 124 bytes per row, 10 GB holds about 80.5 million synthetic orders. At 500 bytes per row it holds 20 million. Measure a representative export to estimate your bill.
lesson1.name: Organization
lesson1.title: Give each day its own partition
lesson1.description: Group files by order date so you can work with one day at a time.
lesson1.note: Why did the storage bill barely move?
lesson1.detail: Date folders keep the same records. Extra CSV headers added 196 bytes in the sample. Date filters can help queries skip irrelevant partitions.
lesson2.name: Format
lesson2.title: Keep the same rows in fewer bytes
lesson2.description: Compare portable exports with a format for analytics. The model assumes the converted copy replaces the original.
lesson2.detail: Gzip CSV and Snappy Parquet saved about 82% in this sample. Gzip suits full-file exports. Parquet preserves column types and supports reading selected columns. Keeping both copies adds storage cost.
lesson3.name: Lifecycle management
lesson3.title: Manage archiving and retention
lesson3.description: Choose when to move older data to cheaper archive storage, and when to delete it. Retention defaults to 7 years and can extend to 14 years.
lesson3.note: How do I automate the move?
lesson3.detail: A Lifecycle rule can archive objects under orders/ after 90 days, counted from upload. Objects below 128 KB are skipped by default. Deep Archive has a 180-day minimum and standard restores typically take about 12 hours.
lesson4.name: Cloud provider
lesson4.title: Choose a provider and region
lesson4.description: Compare regional object-storage rates for the same files and lifecycle policy.
lesson4.detail: Rates are a saved snapshot, not a live quote. Iowa and South Carolina currently share the same listed storage rates. GCP Archive has a 365-day minimum; S3 Deep Archive has 180 days. Early deletion and retrieval charges are excluded.
archiveExplanation: Assumes evenly arriving data across your retention window. Archive after 90 days moves records older than 90 days to archive; retention deletes records beyond the selected number of years.
cloudScope: Object storage uses this provider and region. Before stays at S3 Northern Virginia so you can compare. Source service pricing uses its own location, shown in Source.
cloudContext: {{provider}} · {{region}} · Standard {{standard}} / GiB-month · Archive {{archive}} / GiB-month. USD list-price snapshot: Nov 19, 2026.
sourceScope: Separate from the object-storage estimate above; source data and file exports can coexist. Enter actual database size, including indexes. No free tiers or credits deducted. Add backups, transfer, I/O, replicas and other charges under extras.
source.cluster: Cluster quote for this size (USD / month)
source.bigqueryNote: Iowa (us-central1), active logical storage, on-demand queries. 730 hours/month. Uses database size, not CSV compression. Long-term storage and free allowances are not modeled.
source.rdsNote: Northern Virginia, PostgreSQL db.t4g.micro, Single-AZ, gp3 example. Editable rates; 730 hours/month. Storage is the greater of actual size, provisioned size, or 20 GiB. Instance sizing is illustrative.
source.dynamodbNote: Northern Virginia, Standard table class, on-demand, single region. Enter billable request units, not raw request counts; item size and consistency affect units. No CSV compression or archive policy applies.
source.mongodbNote: Atlas Dedicated starts at $56.94/month. This is an editable starting quote, not a rate per GiB. Enter a quote covering your size, provider, region, replicas and tier; increasing size does not automatically resize the cluster.
lesson5.name: Source
lesson5.title: Factor in the source database
lesson5.description: Choose the service storing your source records and enter its workload. The estimate appears below the object-storage comparison.
lesson5.detail: RDS is relational, MongoDB and DynamoDB are NoSQL, and BigQuery is an analytics warehouse. They serve different workloads. Their compute, indexes and billing units are not interchangeable with compressed file sizes.
combinedTotal: Monthly total if you keep both source and export
pricingSources: Official pricing sources · USD snapshot checked November 19, 2026. Google hourly storage rates use 730 hours/month. Rates are saved, not live.
gcpLifecycle: Keep recent orders in Google Cloud Storage Standard, then move older objects to Archive. Archive has a 365-day minimum storage duration; early-deletion charges are not included.
gcpArchiveAction: (move older data to Google Cloud Archive)
